over preposition and adverb

classical

Liv. 21.28.1: quatientēs scūta super capita

Traupman 355

super (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative; with the ablative mostly in verse · Wiktionary

over, above, across the top of

Over a thing, moving across it, spreading over it or covering it: super capita, over their heads; super rīpās, over the banks.

Other words

  • suprā (+ accusative) — over, above (higher than)

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Verg. G. 1.364: altam suprā volat ardea nūbem; Traupman 355 · Wiktionary

    Higher than a thing, not touching it (see above).

  • trāns (+ accusative) — over (to the far side of)

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.11.27: quī trāns mare currunt · Wiktionary

    Over a river, a wall, the sea: see across.

Examples

  • Gallī occursant in rīpā cum variīs ululātibus cantūque mōris suī, quatientēs scūta super capita

    the Gauls ran up on the bank with all kinds of howling and their customary chant, shaking their shields over their headsLiv. 21.28.1

  • forte quādam dīvīnitus super rīpās Tiberis effūsus lēnibus stagnīs

    by some chance sent by the gods the Tiber had spread over its banks in still poolsLiv. 1.4.4

  • caelum, nōn animum mūtant, quī trāns mare currunt

    those who rush off over the sea change their sky, not their mindHor. Ep. 1.11.27

  • sōl nōn occidat super īrācundiam vestram

    do not let the sun go down on your angerVulg. Eph. 4.26

See also above, across, on top of, beyond.
